mainEntity.name: Should I convert an existing garage or build a ground-up addition for an in-law suite?

acceptedAnswer.text: A ground-up addition builds an entirely new footprint on a foundation, while a garage conversion repurposes existing interior walls and roof structures. Converting an attached garage often lowers initial structural framing costs and avoids extending into yard setbacks. However, you sacrifice covered parking, and the existing concrete slab typically requires leveling, moisture remediation, and insulation to meet residential building codes. A new ground-up addition requires new site prep, foundation footings, and roof integration, but allows complete freedom in room layout, ceiling height, and window placement.
acceptedAnswer.description: Garage conversions use existing framing but eliminate parking and require slab conditioning. Ground-up additions cost more structurally but provide complete layout freedom.
